source.title: AMI Meeting Corpus ES2002b (scenario design meeting, session b, functional design)
source.attribution: See NOTICE.md in the parent directory.

action_items.text: The Industrial Designer will think about the components concept for the next working session.
action_items.quote: for uh our Industrial Designer, you're gonna be thinking about the components concept.

action_items.text: The User Interface Designer will think about the user interface for the next working session.
action_items.quote: User Interface Designer gonna be thinking about our user interface

action_items.text: Marketing will do trend watching for the next working session.
action_items.quote: and marketing you're gonna be thinking about trend watching.

action_items.text: The project manager (Speaker_1) will put the minutes of this meeting into the project documents folder.
action_items.quote: so I'll be putting the minutes of this uh this meeting into the project documents folder

decisions.text: Target the product at the fifteen to thirty five age bracket.
decisions.quote: Are we all happy about the idea of um aiming the product at um the fifteen to thirty five bracket?

decisions.text: Keep the function set to the most basic: on/off, channel up/down, volume up/down, and direct channel selection by number.
decisions.quote: the the most basic stuff possible. Um on off, up and down channels, up and down volume and uh skip to a channel.

decisions.text: Stay with regular batteries rather than a rechargeable/charging-dock design.
decisions.quote: Okay, so just stick to to regular

decisions.text: Adopt the three-bucket categorisation of controls (audio, video, device) as the working frame.
decisions.quote: that we'll u use this idea David's proposed, where we think of these three sort of buckets

notes: Fairly clear on the three or four settled points (target age group, basic function set, regular batteries, three control buckets), and the wrap-up gives role-level assignments for the next working session; individual commitments are otherwise thin. Left out: speech recognition (explicitly deferred, 'if we can'), infra-red and TV-only (company requirements or PM suggestion, not group-agreed), mute button (one participant's suggestion, only tacitly accepted), and the hidden-drawer/grouped controls idea (floated, only later folded into the buckets decision). The batteries decision is settled by the project manager's 'just stick to to regular' and a 'Yeah.'; the age-bracket quote is the proposing question, with the agreement in the next utterance.
